lente.que_es: A fixed lens with optical zoom: it can't be swapped, but it brings the image closer without losing quality. The hood is the visor at the front.
lente.para_que: The lens frames and focuses. On its left side are the AF/MF button, to choose auto or manual focus, and the FOCUS/ZOOM switch, which sets whether the ring focuses or zooms.
lente.tip: Autofocus recognizes faces very quickly, but the CPMA recommends shooting in manual most of the time.
lente.foto_pie: The Z90V with its fixed lens and hood

nd.que_es: Built-in “sunglasses” that sit inside the camera, behind the lens.
nd.para_que: When there's a lot of light or you shoot outdoors, it cuts light so the image doesn't blow out. It's controlled with the ND switch on the back: each step up darkens the image a little more.
nd.tip: Raise the ND first, then finish adjusting with the iris.
nd.foto_pie: Back of the camera: ND switch, AUTO/MANUAL and REC button

sensor.que_es: A chip that receives light and turns it into a digital image.
sensor.para_que: It's large for a camera this size, so it looks good in low light. It also powers the hybrid autofocus, which has 273 reference points.
sensor.tip: Even with a good sensor, it's always better to light the scene well.

pantalla.que_es: The LCD screen on the left side and the viewfinder at the back, where you put your eye.
pantalla.para_que: Opening the screen turns the camera on and reveals the control buttons and the card slots. The viewfinder helps in sunlight, when the screen is hard to see.
pantalla.tip: Resting your eye on the viewfinder also helps you hold the camera steadier.
pantalla.foto_pie: Screen open: the buttons and SD slots are behind it

cuerpo.que_es: The central box with the camera's “brain” and most of its buttons.
cuerpo.para_que: Next to the screen are power, WHITE BALANCE and MENU. Below, IRIS, ISO and SHUTTER for exposure. On the back, the multi-selector to move through the menu and the AUTO/MANUAL switch.
cuerpo.tip: If you can't change anything in AUTO, move the switch on the back to MANUAL.
cuerpo.foto_pie: Button panel on the left side

audio.que_es: The top handle is removable. It has two XLR inputs for professional microphones, their INPUT switches, the zoom lever and a second REC button. There's a built-in microphone at the front.
audio.para_que: With an external microphone on XLR you record clear voices. The built-in microphone captures ambient sound.
audio.tip: For supporting shots, switch back to the internal mic so the interviewee's voice doesn't sneak in.
audio.foto_pie: XLR inputs at the front of the handle

memoria.que_es: Two SD card slots under a small door behind the screen, and the ports to connect cables.
memoria.para_que: Your video is saved on the card. Cables send the image to a TV or a live broadcast.
memoria.tip: Insert the card following the shape on the guide until it clicks.

bateria.que_es: The camera's power source. It goes on the back, under the viewfinder.
bateria.para_que: It powers everything. To attach it, slide the lock at the bottom and insert the battery with the connectors facing up; release the lock and it's secure.
bateria.tip: Always carry a charged spare battery.
bateria.foto_pie: Attaching the battery on the back
